quarterly_data.quarter: Kohoku Kogyo annual securities report: FY2025 (03-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Optical Components and Devices, FY2025 (management's analysis): submarine-cable optical device sales saw a short-term adjustment early in the year from schedule changes on some projects and inventory adjustment of existing products as customers switched to compact products, then rose step by step from spring; new submarine-cable projects increased and compact optical isolators were increasingly adopted. With generative AI driving data-center investment, supply and demand for Faraday rotators stayed tight, so the company increased production capacity to meet rising orders. The company states it holds a high global market share in optical isolators for submarine cables, with 25-year maintenance-free reliability on the seabed.

quarterly_data.quarter: Kohoku Kogyo annual securities report: FY2025 (03-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Lead Terminals for aluminum electrolytic capacitors (annual securities report): the company supplies every Japanese aluminum electrolytic capacitor maker and is expanding sales to Taiwanese, Korean and Chinese makers; it states it holds a high market share in the automotive (drivetrain) market and in AI servers, where demand for hybrid and conductive-polymer capacitors is rising quickly. In FY2025 it continued to expand capacity at its Dongguan (China) plant and continued developing laser welding technology. Target: keep improving the earnings structure to establish a business that stably maintains an operating margin of 10% or more in Lead Terminals.
quarterly_data.figure: target operating margin of 10% or more (Lead Terminals)

quarterly_data.quarter: Kohoku Kogyo annual securities report: FY2025 (03-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D (annual securities report): FY2025 R&D expenses JPY 641 million (Lead Terminals JPY 114 million, Optical Components and Devices JPY 526 million), 39 R&D staff at year-end, all at the parent. Optical themes: magneto-optic single-crystal Faraday rotators; high-reliability optical devices and modules for higher-speed, higher-capacity submarine cables; devices for multicore fiber; next-generation devices related to silicon photonics; SSG high-purity quartz glass parts; optical isolators and filters for satellite communications; PLZT devices such as optical modulators for photonics-electronics convergence. Results: started sample shipments of optical devices combining an optical isolator with an optical filter and of optical modules with other functions; developed an optical device combining fan-in/fan-out with an optical isolator for multicore fiber; strengthened the SSG lineup including lenses for semiconductor manufacturing equipment and advanced development of specialty fiber preforms, with inquiries rising from optical fiber makers. Management plans R&D on multicore fiber looking 10 years or more ahead and product development for space communications, and is building full mass production of SSG products on rising inquiries from semiconductor equipment makers and optical fiber makers.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D expenses JPY 641 million (optical JPY 526 million)
